learning_outcomes.text: Knows the basic concepts of thermodynamics and energy conversions. Uses the zeroth law of thermodynamics for temperature and thermal equilibrium relationships.
Knows the properties of pure substances. Relates phase changes and material properties. Determines and calculates state variables.
Applies pressure, temperature, and specific volume relations for gases. Determines properties with the ideal gas equation and calculates work done in state changes.

Applies the first law of thermodynamics to cycles, closed and open systems, and performs system analysis. Calculates heat and work relations, mass and energy balances. Determines heat and work relations for cycles in closed systems.
Defines the second law of thermodynamics, applies it to a cycle and heat pumps, calculates cycle efficiency and performance coefficients.
Defines and determines entropy and entropy change. Demonstrates the principle of increase of entropy and applies it to thermodynamic systems.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION AND BASIC CONCEPTS: Thermodynamics and energy, importance of dimensions and units
Systems and control volumes, state changes and cycles, zeroth law of thermodynamics, pressure
ENERGY CONVERSIONS AND GENERAL ENERGY ANALYSIS: Forms of energy, energy transfer by heat and work, mechanical energy, first law of thermodynamics and energy conversion efficiencies
PROPERTIES OF PURE SUBSTANCES: Pure substance, phase change processes of pure substances, property diagrams and property tables for phase change processes
Ideal gas equation of state, compressibility factor
ENERGY ANALYSIS OF CLOSED SYSTEMS: Moving boundary work, energy balance for closed systems
Specific heats, internal energy, enthalpy and specific heats of ideal gases, solids and liquids
MASS AND ENERGY ANALYSIS FOR CONTROL VOLUMES: Principle of conservation of mass, flow work and energy of fluid
Energy analysis in steady-flow open systems and time-varying open systems
SECOND LAW OF THERMODYNAMICS: Heat and energy reservoirs, heat engines, refrigeration machines and heat pumps
Reversible and irreversible processes, Carnot principles, thermodynamic temperature scale, Carnot machines (heat and refrigeration machines, heat pump)
ENTROPY: Principle of increase of entropy, entropy change of pure substances, isentropic processes
Tds relations, entropy change of liquids and solids - ideal gases
Isentropic efficiencies of steady-flow machines and entropy balance

assessment_methods.method: Contribution to success during the year

assessment_rules: The overall assessment is based on a midterm exam (80%) and a quiz (20%) for the in-term work, which accounts for 50% of the final grade. The final exam contributes the remaining 50% to the overall grade.
